key_insight: The paper turns aggregation-diffusion PDEs into a variational optimal-control problem and learns a neural velocity field to transport densities while respecting the underlying physics.
engineering_relevance: This offers a physics-informed surrogate for complex transport-driven materials and biological dynamics, enabling faster simulation of nonlocal nonlinear density evolution.
method: Reformulate the PDE using the Onsager variational principle with velocity as the control variable.
Evolve the density with a continuity equation along particle trajectories and train a neural network on the variational objective.
Couple density and generalized score equations, then use Euler time stepping for efficient loss evaluation and error analysis.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments on several representative models, showing accuracy and effectiveness, alongside a theoretical error decomposition and bounds.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of time discretization, Monte Carlo sampling, and neural approximation, so stability and generalization should be checked carefully in new regimes.
paper_title: Variational neural transport for aggregation-diffusion equations
